method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); three regulative rules (service of originating process, the defence, payment under an accepted offer) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Uniform Civil Procedure Rules 2005 (NSW) (2005-418), corpus document nsw_legislation:2025-02-03/sl-2005-0418 from the Open Australian Legal Corpus (collected 10 March 2025; unofficial, possibly out of date), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/sl-2005-0418.txt (text_sha256 0493f0aa73f5087904e6416d671fd42d6b0c3a82e5c33fb9e5cf446630f8e955 per the meta file)
license: Apache-2.0 for the L4; the quoted rules are from the New South Wales Legislation website, CC BY 4.0, via the Open Australian Legal Corpus (CC BY 4.0); see SOURCE-LICENSE.md
seat: the claimant (plaintiff) bringing a civil claim, such as a personal injury, compensation, debt or other money claim, in a NSW court

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run ucpr-time.l4 ; l4 run ucpr-proceedings.l4 ; l4 run ucpr-offers-costs.l4 ; l4 run ucpr-cases-proceedings.l4 ; l4 run ucpr-cases-offers-costs.l4
checks.result: 172 assertions written, 172 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read (a deliberately wrong assertion was checked to be reported as failed). Expected values worked by hand from the text, with a calendar for days of the week.

scope: Focus: the provisions a claimant meets. In: r 1.11 (reckoning of time), r 1.12 (extension, as an input); r 6.2 (commencement and service of originating process); r 12.1, 12.3, 12.4 (discontinuance); r 12.8, 12.9 (dismissal for lack of progress); r 14.3, 14.4 (defence and reply times); r 15.12-15.14(4), 15.17 (particulars in personal injury and death claims); r 16.1-16.10 (default judgment); r 20.25-20.29 (offers of compromise); r 23.1-23.3 (medical examination expenses); r 36.7 (interest); r 42.1 (as the fallback), 42.13-42.17, 42.19, 42.20, 42.34, 42.35 (costs). Out: the rest of the 59 Parts and the Schedules (procedure addressed to the court or registry, form of documents, evidence, discovery, subpoenas, enforcement, specialist lists and particular Acts). Reasons in NOTES.md.
